rivals.statement: On HumanEval+/MBPP+ most of the gap between the cued base and RL-Code is broken answer contracts, not wrong logic: cap hits, no final python block, or a block that does not parse or lacks what the tests call. Code-RL's top-8 directions write that contract, which is low-rank, so at 1x they close most of the gap (cap hits 27->9, no block 34->8). Math's directions write only the generic part (finishing, a closing block), so they fix less.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers sized the code edit from the math dial, where the gap is mostly reliability and capability and 8 directions close about two thirds of it on hard328. On code a larger share of the gap is contract failures, and a rank-8 edit removes those almost entirely. This fits result-6e4536 (Math's directions remove no-block endings and box nothing) and result-124593 (the math dial also adds skill; this claim is only about how the code gap is made up). run-06/f2-m03 forecast this cell well although its cause is refuted. Code-RL's change really is concentrated (top-8 share 0.174), but General-RL concentrates as much, so the concentration was not caused by a gradable reward. What f2-m03 picked up is that the concentrated directions hold the contract.

holds_against.why: The L11-21 band passes 366 with 6 cap hits / 9 no-block vs L0-10 372 with 12 / 17. The band that fixes more contract failures passes 6 fewer, but 6 problems is inside one-sample noise (about +-13). Both bands beat random (72 contract failures) by 35-41, in line with their 43-57 fewer contract failures. The late band fixes no contract failures (34/40) and adds nothing (342), as the mechanism says.

Math directions at 1.5x on code pass 368 with 6 no-block, vs Code 1.5x 399. No-block endings are only the generic part of the contract. Math's directions do not set code's entry point, stdin/stdout convention or test-free final block, so they recover about half of what Code's directions do.

forecasts.reason: Code 1x already saturates the contract and Math adds only generic finishing, so the sum sits near the Code 1.5x level (399); the earlier 411 was a high draw.
Same cell as t03 at another seed, seed SD about 8.
RL-Code holds the full contract plus logic; 401 replicates with seed noise.
As t05.
The contract fix is near-deterministic per problem, so Code 1x replicates 386 (dial 386/399/394).
As t07.
Think-SFT was never trained on this reward's contract: long reasoning means more cap hits and extra or test-laden blocks under the raw Code prompt, so it loses about 40 to contract failures.
The Math cue does not supply the code contract either (base: Math cue 326 vs Code cue 317), so it scores close to t15.
Math's top-8 input subspace reads math-answer contract text (equations, answer lines) that code answers lack, so code text drives it well below math text (spec's 0.54 is nearby).
A random rank-8 subspace reads generic activation energy, which code and math text share.

direct_test.claim: The base failures that Code-top8-1x fixes are enriched for answer-contract failures (cap hit, no final python block, a final block that fails to parse or lacks the entry point the tests call) well beyond what a resample fixes.
direct_test.computation: 1. Load per-problem rows of base + Code cue (code1/base_cue-01, seed 51000000) and of the code_dial cells 'Code directions 1x' and 'random rank-8 1.5x' (same seed); join on problem id (538). 2. For each problem the base fails, classify the base answer as a contract failure if: cap_hit; or no ```python (or ```) block after the last reasoning; or the last block fails ast.parse; or, for function tasks, the test's entry-point name is not defined by a def in the block; or, for stdio tasks, the block never reads stdin. Otherwise it is a logic failure. Use the ending-01 block parser for the no-block test. 3. F_top8 = base failed and top8-1x passed; F_rand = base failed and random passed. 4. S_top8 = contract share of F_top8; S_rand = contract share of F_rand. r_c = |F_top8 among contract failures| / |contract failures|; r_l = the same for logic failures. 5. 90 % bootstrap over problems (10,000 draws) for S_top8, S_top8 - S_rand and r_c / r_l.
direct_test.refuted_if: S_top8 < 0.50, or the 90 % lower bound of S_top8 - S_rand is <= 0, or r_c / r_l < 2.0
direct_test.null: The random rank-8 1.5x edit at the same seed (in effect a fresh base sample), whose fixes give the contract share expected from resampling. Also the contract share among all base failures (about 61 of 221 from cap hits and no-block alone).

rivals.statement: HumanEval+/MBPP+ are easy for the cued base: most problems it fails in one sample it passes in others, so the code gap is almost all per-sample reliability. Code-RL's top-8 directions lower the per-step error rate on reasoning text everywhere, as Math's dial does on finished-wrong math (result-124593). On a set whose gap is reliability, that recovers nearly all of RL's gain. On hard328, where a third of the gap needs answers the base never writes, it recovers less.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers took the share of RL's gain that 8 directions close from hard328 (about two thirds), where much of the gap is capability: the base has no right sample on 26 of 36 vote-gap problems. On code the gap is nearly all reliability, so the same kind of edit closes 82 % of it. This fits result-124593 (the dial adds right answers on base finished-wrong problems as RL does), result-6e4536 (no boxed displacement), and the refutations of incomplete switching (result-d02d46) and bf16 under-application (result-c2edfb). run-06/f2-m03 forecast this cell well although its cause is refuted. Code-RL's update is concentrated (0.174), as General-RL's is, so concentration is not caused by a gradable reward. What f2-m03 captured is that the concentrated directions carry the reliability shift.

holds_against.why: Code 1x cuts cap hits 27->9 (and no-block answers 34->8). This looks like a contract fix. But cap hits and missing blocks are per-sample events: the base finishes with a block on most of those problems in other samples (Math-cue cell 326). They are reliability of finishing, and the net gain of 69 exceeds the 44 those two categories could give.

On hard328 the base has a right sample on only 10 of 36 problems where RL's vote wins. That is the capability-heavy hard set, where the edit closes only about 2/3. The mechanism predicts the closed share follows the base-solvable share of the gap, which is high on easy code.

forecasts.reason: Math's directions add reliability on code too (368 vs random 331), partly adding to Code's; the 411 draw shrinks toward about 405.
As t03, another seed.
RL-Code 401 replicates within seed SD of about 8.
As t05.
The dial cells 386/399/394 fit one true rate near 390, and 386 was a slightly low draw.
As t07.
Think-SFT is a reliable reasoner (ties RL on MATH-500, beats it out of domain 342 vs 332). On an easy, reliability-bound set it reaches RL-Code's level.
Reliability does not depend on the cue (base: Math cue 326 vs Code cue 317), so this lands at t15's level.
The directions act on generic reasoning steps ('Okay', checks, derivations) that code answers contain in the same register; drive barely varies across texts (CV 6.8 %, result-0b3807).
A random subspace reads generic activation energy, which is shared across domains.

direct_test.claim: The base failures that Code-top8-1x fixes are mostly problems the base passes in its other stored base-like samples, clearly more than base failures in general.
direct_test.computation: 1. Load per-problem pass/fail of base + Code cue (code1/base_cue-01), base + Math cue (code1/base_mathcue-01), the code_dial cells 'random rank-8 1.5x' and 'Code directions 1x', and RL-Code plain (code1/rl_plain-01); join on problem id (538). 2. k2 = passes in the two base-like cells (Math cue, random 1.5x), from 0 to 2. 3. Among problems the Code-cue base fails: F_top8 = passed by top8-1x; Q_top8 = share of F_top8 with k2 >= 1; Q_base = share of all Code-cue base failures with k2 >= 1; Q_RL = share of RL-Code's fixes with k2 >= 1. 4. Fix rate of top8-1x within k2 = 0 and within k2 >= 1. 5. 90 % bootstrap over problems (10,000 draws) for Q_top8 and Q_top8 - Q_base.
direct_test.refuted_if: Q_top8 < 0.60, or the 90 % lower bound of Q_top8 - Q_base is <= 0.10
direct_test.threshold: Q_top8 >= 0.60 and Q_top8 - Q_base lower bound > 0.10
direct_test.null: The share of base-solvable problems among all base failures (Q_base, which is what fixes drawn without regard to base solvability would give). Also RL-Code's own fixes (Q_RL) as the reference for a full reliability-plus-capability change.
